indicator_definition: The energy import dependency rate shows the extent to which an economy relies on energy imports to meet its energy needs. It is calculated as net energy imports divided by gross inland energy consumption, expressed as a percentage. A higher rate means greater dependence on imported energy.
rationale: High energy import dependency exposes economies to energy supply disruptions and price volatility. Reducing dependency through energy efficiency and renewable energy development supports energy security and sustainability. Progress means a reduction in the energy import dependency rate.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics submitted under EU energy statistics regulations. Gross inland energy consumption covers all energy needed to meet domestic demand. Net imports are calculated as imports minus exports and stock changes.
